title: Products of distinguished triangles are distinguished
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a pre-triangulated category [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Let $J$ be a set and let $T_j=(X_j\to Y_j\to Z_j\to X_j[1])$ be distinguished triangles for $j\in J$. Assume the products of the $X_j$, $Y_j$, $Z_j$, and $X_j[1]$ exist [def-weil-category-product]. Then the componentwise product triangle $\prod X_j\to\prod Y_j\to\prod Z_j\to(\prod X_j)[1]$ is distinguished, with the last arrow using the canonical product/shift isomorphism.

proof.text: Apply Mathlib CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.productTriangle_distinguished to the family T. This is exactly Stacks 0CRG(2)(a): complete the product of first arrows to a distinguished triangle, extend each pair of projections by TR3, and assemble the third components by the product universal property. Hom exactness and exact products of abelian groups show that the resulting third component is an isomorphism, so transport the distinguished triangle along it. The shift autoequivalence preserves the product, giving the required last arrow.
